predecessors.name: Old Kingdom of Norway
predecessors.text: Norway, with Iceland and the other Norwegian dependencies

successors.name: Denmark-Norway
successors.text: Denmark and Norway, with Iceland, Faroe Islands, Gotland, Scania, Blekinge and Halland

ledger.x: 17 June 1397: the Kalmar Union is proclaimed.
1408: the Teutonic Order sells Gotland to Denmark.
1426: war with Holstein and the Hanseatic League begins.
1429: Cliopatria drops the Greenland cells from the union's shape.
17 July 1435: the Peace of Vordingborg ends the Holstein war.
17 July 1435: Schleswig passes to the count of Holstein.
20 June 1448: Sweden elects its own king, Karl Knutsson, and the union is broken.
1 September 1448: the House of Oldenburg takes the Danish throne.
February 1449: Norway splits between Christian and Karl Knutsson.
August 1450: Christian is crowned king of Norway.
23 June 1457: Christian I becomes king of Sweden.
5 March 1460: Christian I is confirmed Duke of Schleswig and Count of Holstein.
23 June 1464: Christian I loses Sweden.
1472: Scotland annexes Orkney and Shetland.
6 October 1497: Hans wins Sweden.
August 1501: Sweden renounces Hans.
November 1520: Christian II is crowned king of Sweden.
January 1521: the Swedish War of Liberation begins.
June 1523: Gustav Vasa takes Stockholm.
6 June 1523: the Kalmar Union ends.

wars.name: War with Holstein and the Hanseatic League (1426-1435)
wars.outcome: Eric lost the South Jutland lands he had won; the Peace of Vordingborg (17 July 1435) ceded Schleswig to the count of Holstein and exempted the Hanseatic cities from the Sound Dues.

wars.name: Engelbrekt rebellion
wars.outcome: A national and social rebellion of Swedish farmers and mine workers; it led to Eric's overthrow in Denmark and Sweden in 1439 and in Norway in 1442.

wars.name: Contest for Norway between Christian I and Karl Knutsson
wars.outcome: Karl was crowned at Trondheim on 20 November 1449 and forced in June 1450 to renounce Norway; Christian was crowned there on 2 August 1450.

wars.name: Battle of Brunkeberg
wars.outcome: Christian's 'final attempt to regain Sweden ended in total military failure at the Battle of Brunkeberg (outside Stockholm) October 1471' against Sten Sture the Elder.

wars.name: Hans's conquest of Sweden
wars.outcome: Rotebro (28 September 1497), the settlement at Klara Priory (6 October) and Hans's entry into Stockholm: Sten Sture relinquished the regency.

wars.name: Swedish revolt against Hans
wars.outcome: Sture and the council renounced allegiance in August 1501; Queen Christina surrendered Stockholm on 5 May 1502.

wars.name: War of Hans against Sweden and Lübeck
wars.outcome: 'Between 1510 and 1512, the king waged a final war with both Sweden and Lübeck'; no territorial result is stated.

wars.name: Christian II's wars with Sten Sture the Younger
wars.outcome: Failures in 1517 (Vedila) and 1518 (Brännkyrka); in 1520 a large army of French, German and Scottish mercenaries won, Sture was mortally wounded at Bogesund on 19 January 1520 and Christian was crowned in Stockholm in November 1520.

wars.name: Swedish War of Liberation
wars.outcome: Swedish victory: Kalmar fell on 27 May 1523, Gustav Vasa was proclaimed king on 6 June and Stockholm taken on 17 June 1523; the Treaty of Malmö of 1 September 1524 formalised the secession.

certainty.note: The union's northern frontiers (Lapland, the Finnish and Karelian marches against Novgorod and Moscow) are approximate throughout and Cliopatria draws Sweden and Finland only in part before 1429; the Danish coasts are firm.
